title: March Wedding Guest Dresses
metaTitle: March Wedding Guest Dresses: Dressing for a Month of Two Seasons
metaDescription: March wedding guest dresses for a month that can feel like winter in Chicago and summer in Miami: climate data by city, sleeves, fabrics, colours and what to bring for the evening.
h1: March Wedding Guest Dresses for a Month That Can't Decide
intro:
March wedding guest dresses have a harder job than the dresses for almost any other month. Spring has officially started by the end of it, the shops are full of pastel chiffon, and yet in much of the northern United States the average March afternoon still tops out in the forties. Meanwhile a March wedding in Phoenix or Miami can be warmer than an October one in Chicago. The month is not one season; it is several, depending on the city on the invitation.

That makes March the month where checking the weather properly pays off most. Below is real climate data for ten U.S. cities, what it means for sleeves, fabric and length, and how to pick a dress that looks like spring without leaving you cold at nine in the evening.

contentSections.heading: Ten Cities, Three Different Months
contentSections.content:
NOAA's 1991–2020 U.S. Climate Normals are the federal record of what a typical month looks like at a weather station, averaged over thirty years. For March, they split the country into three rough groups.

Average March high / low (°F) and March rainfall, NOAA 1991–2020 U.S. Climate Normals:

Chicago O'Hare — 47.0° / 31.0° — 2.45 in
New York, Central Park — 49.9° / 35.8° — 4.29 in
Philadelphia — 52.8° / 34.3° — 3.96 in
Seattle–Tacoma — 54.2° / 39.9° — 4.17 in
Charlotte — 64.2° / 41.2° — 3.95 in
Atlanta — 65.9° / 45.3° — 4.68 in
Los Angeles (LAX) — 66.1° / 52.2° — 1.73 in
Dallas–Fort Worth — 68.6° / 47.8° — 3.30 in
Phoenix — 78.1° / 54.5° — 0.83 in
Miami — 80.6° / 65.6° — 2.46 in

The northern cities — Chicago, New York, Philadelphia, Seattle — have March highs between 47 and 54 degrees and lows between 31 and 40. That is a winter-weight wedding, whatever the calendar says. Long sleeves, a heavier fabric and a real coat for arrivals and departures are the sensible default.

The Southeast and Texas — Charlotte, Atlanta, Dallas–Fort Worth — have highs in the mid-sixties but lows in the low to high forties, and the gap between afternoon and night is the widest in the table: about 21 degrees in Atlanta and Dallas–Fort Worth, 23 in Charlotte. An afternoon ceremony can be pleasant in a midi with light sleeves; the reception after dark is a jacket-and-tights evening.

The warm cities — Phoenix, Miami and, more mildly, Los Angeles — are already in spring or early summer. Phoenix's average March high is 78.1 degrees with less than an inch of rain for the month; Miami's is 80.6 degrees with a low of 65.6. Short sleeves, lighter fabrics and outdoor-friendly lengths are all reasonable there.

The point of the table is not the exact number for your city but the habit: look up the station nearest the venue before buying. The same NOAA dataset covers thousands of U.S. weather stations.

contentSections.heading: Sleeves Are the First Decision
contentSections.content:
For most March weddings outside the warm cities, sleeves matter more than any other feature of the dress. A cold arm at an outdoor ceremony or a draughty reception hall is the thing guests notice most and fix least gracefully.

Long sleeves in a sheer fabric — chiffon or mesh — are the most useful March compromise. They look light and spring-like in photographs and still give some warmth. Many of the floral maxi dresses in the shop below use exactly this construction.

Three-quarter and elbow sleeves suit the in-between cities. They leave the wrist free for a bracelet and keep the dress from looking wintry.

Short, flutter or cap sleeves are best kept for the warm-city weddings, or for indoor venues where you will not spend much time outside. If you love a sleeveless dress, buy the wrap or jacket at the same time.

The long sleeve wedding guest dresses page and the wedding guest dresses with sleeves page have more options in both lengths.

contentSections.heading: Fabric: Spring Colours, Not Necessarily Spring Weights
contentSections.content:
The mistake that makes March guests cold is choosing a summer fabric because it comes in a spring colour. The colour can be spring; the weight should suit the forecast.

Crepe and heavier satin hold their shape, block wind and look polished from day to night. A satin midi in sage, dusty blue or lilac is a strong March choice for any of the colder cities.

Lined chiffon and tulle over a lining give the floaty look of spring with more warmth than a single layer. Check product descriptions for the word "lined", especially on lighter colours, where an unlined skirt can be more transparent in daylight.

Knit midi dresses in a fine gauge are underrated for March: they are warm, they travel without creasing and they work at dressy casual and many semi-formal weddings.

Pure cotton, linen and single-layer rayon are the summer fabrics to leave for April and May in the north, though they are reasonable for Phoenix or Miami.

contentSections.heading: Colour Without the Costume
contentSections.content:
March is the month when pastels feel right again, and there is no reason to avoid them. Dusty blue, sage, lilac, blush and butter yellow all read as spring without being as loud as summer brights. Muted floral prints on a darker ground — navy, deep green, slate — bridge the gap well for an evening reception in a cold city.

Two cautions apply in March as in every month. White, ivory and very pale champagne are best avoided because they can compete with the bride in photographs. And very pale pastels in thin fabric can photograph as white under a flash, so check the shade in daylight.

If you are going to more than one wedding this spring, a sage or dusty blue midi with sheer long sleeves is one of the most re-wearable choices: it works from March through May and at most dress codes short of black tie. The spring wedding guest dresses page and the colour hub cover the full palette.

contentSections.heading: How Each Dress Code Translates to March
contentSections.content:
The dress code on the invitation sets the formality; March sets the warmth. Putting the two together gives a clear starting point for each code. The garment lists below come from the Emily Post Institute's attire guide; the March adjustments are about weather.

Black tie — Emily Post lists a "formal (floor length) evening gown", a "dressy cocktail dress" or "your dressiest 'little black dress'". In March, a floor-length gown is the warmer of those options as well as the most formal. Velvet is still entirely appropriate in the colder cities; satin with long sleeves or a matching wrap works everywhere else.

Black tie optional — the same gown or dressy cocktail dress, with "dressy separates" also listed. A long satin skirt with a fine-knit or silk long-sleeved top is a smart March answer: formal, warm and easy to move in.

Semi-formal — a "short afternoon or cocktail dress", a "little black dress", a "long dressy skirt and top" or dressy separates. Emily Post adds that if the event runs past 6 in the evening, you should "err on the side of formality". In March, a midi in crepe or lined chiffon with sleeves covers both the formality and the cold.

Dressy casual — Emily Post lists a dress, a skirt and dressy top, a dressy pants outfit, or nice jeans with a dressy top. For a wedding, a dress or a dressy pants outfit is the safer reading. A fine-knit midi dress with boots is a March-specific option that looks considered rather than casual.

Casual — a sundress or a skirt are on the list. In the warm cities they are exactly right; in the north, a casual March wedding is a good place for a long-sleeved jersey or knit dress and a jacket.

The dress code guide explains every code in more detail, from casual to white tie.

contentSections.heading: Planning the Evening, Not Just the Ceremony
contentSections.content:
In the colder half of the table, the evening matters more than the afternoon. Average lows in the thirties in Chicago, New York and Philadelphia, and in the forties in Atlanta and Dallas–Fort Worth, mean the walk from the reception to the car is the coldest part of the day.

A few things make the difference. Bring a coat you are happy to be photographed in, because exit photos happen outdoors. Sheer tights in a skin tone or black are entirely acceptable with a midi or maxi in March. Closed-toe shoes or a block heel help on wet ground; NOAA's normals put March rainfall at around four inches in New York, Philadelphia, Seattle, Charlotte and Atlanta, so a damp lawn is likely at an outdoor venue. And if the reception is in a tent, ask whether it will be heated.

The wedding guest cover-ups and wraps page lists layers that look deliberate rather than borrowed.

contentSections.heading: What's in the Shop Below
contentSections.content: The dresses here were pulled from Amazon's product API on 12 October 2026, from searches for long-sleeve, pastel, floral and satin spring wedding guest dresses, with duplicates removed. On that date, the 30 listings ran from $23.99 to $64.99, with a median of $47.49; 29 of the 30 were under $60. Most are midi or maxi length, and many use sheer long sleeves or floral prints — the combination that suits a March wedding in a colder city. Prices and stock are checked daily and listings that lose their price drop out automatically, so the grid you see may differ.

faqs.question: What should I wear to a March wedding?
faqs.answer: Check the climate where the wedding is. In northern cities, average March highs are in the forties and fifties, so long sleeves, a heavier fabric and a coat are sensible. In the Southeast and Texas, expect a mild afternoon and a cool evening. Phoenix and Miami are already warm enough for short sleeves.

faqs.question: Can I wear a sleeveless dress to a March wedding?
faqs.answer: Yes, at an indoor venue or in a warm city, but bring a wrap or jacket for the ceremony and the evening. In Chicago, New York or Philadelphia, average March lows are in the thirties.

faqs.question: Are pastel colours appropriate for a March wedding?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dusty blue, sage, lilac, blush and butter yellow all suit March. Avoid shades pale enough to photograph as white, and choose a fabric weight that suits the forecast rather than the colour.

faqs.question: Is velvet too heavy for a March wedding?
faqs.answer: Not in the colder cities. With average March highs between 47 and 54 degrees in Chicago, New York, Philadelphia and Seattle, velvet is still comfortable, especially for an evening or black tie wedding. In Phoenix, Miami or Los Angeles it will feel heavy.

faqs.question: What shoes work for a March wedding?
faqs.answer: Closed-toe heels, block heels or dressy ankle boots in the colder cities, especially if any part of the day is outdoors on grass. Sandals suit the warm cities and indoor venues. Bring flats for the evening if you expect to dance.

faqs.question: Should I wear tights to a March wedding?
faqs.answer: Sheer tights are acceptable with a midi or maxi dress at a March wedding, and in colder cities they are often the comfortable choice for the evening.
